en-US.description: Modern Windows system toolkit — network monitor, performance tuning, cleanup, battery health, process manager, and more.
en-US.longDescription:
SysManager is a modern Windows system toolkit built with WPF and .NET 10.
It provides a comprehensive set of tools in a single application including
live network monitoring, ping and traceroute, speed tests, performance tuning
with power plan management, deep disk cleanup, duplicate file finder, disk
analyzer, battery health monitoring, process manager, app uninstaller,
startup control, Windows services manager, Windows features manager, driver
information, and system health overview.
en-US.name: SysManager
en-US.releaseNotes:
[1.136.169] - 2026-11-12
File Shredder refuses to shred a whole drive, your profile or one of your own folders such as Downloads, and a file
deep in a folder tree is now removed after its overwrite instead of being left behind.
Fixed
- File Shredder refused Windows, System32 and Program Files and anything inside them, but not a folder that holds
  them, so the root of a drive passed its check, and so did the profile folder, AppData, ProgramData and your own
  folders (Documents, Downloads, Desktop and the rest). A shred of one of those after a question that counted one
  item destroyed everything in it. They are now refused as a whole, together with any folder that holds one of them;
  the files and folders inside them can still be shredded. A drive root has passed since the File Shredder came in 1.4.0.
- A file whose path has 260 characters or more was overwritten and then left on disk: the overwrite reached it, but
  the shredder's own removal, its named-stream search and two of its path checks took the path in a form Windows
  limits to 259 characters unless long paths are turned on. Every one of those calls now uses the long form when a
  path needs it. The removal has been that way since 1.136.164 and the named-stream search since 1.131.8.
- A file refused partway through a folder shred, for a reason found before its first byte was written, stopped the
  whole folder with only that reason, and the files already destroyed went unreported. It is now left in place and
  named with the others the shred could not reach, the message says how many were destroyed, and the folders above
  it are left as they are.
- A folder whose real location could not be read is refused before anything in it is touched, rather than checked
  only by the name it was picked by.
Changed
- On a PC without long paths turned on, a folder whose path has 260 characters or more is now checked for links and
  walked like any other: Disk Analyzer, Duplicate Finder, Large Files, the cleanup sweeps and the leftover search
  refused it as one whose real location could not be read.
Verify the download
Get-FileHash .\SysManager-v1.136.169.exe -Algorithm SHA256
Expected SHA256: D6BB7B04E993E2AF347CD096873389E8557038433BA55DE95AE970A70D251B7F
This build is not code-signed, so Windows will warn on first launch. That is
expected for a small independent app: see what the warning says and what to
click.
Code signing is planned through the SignPath Foundation,
which provides free certificates to open-source projects, with signing performed by
SignPath.io. Until then, the SHA256 above and the build
attestation below are what establish that a download is the genuine build.
Code signing policy
This release is not code-signed. The team roles, release-approval process and
privacy policy required by the SignPath Foundation programme
are documented in advance under Code signing
policy. That
documentation is a prerequisite for applying, not evidence of a certificate. The
attribution line naming SignPath as the signing provider will appear here once a
certificate is actually issued.
This program will not transfer any information to other networked systems unless
specifically requested by the user or the person installing or operating it. Two checks
run on their own when SysManager starts: the version check against the GitHub Releases
API, at most once a day, and the Dashboard's app-updates alert, which asks winget. The
About tab can switch off either. Everything else that uses the network runs only when you
use it. Full
privacy policy.
Verify where this binary came from
This exe was built by GitHub Actions from this public source, and the build is
recorded in the Sigstore public transparency log. With the
GitHub CLI:
gh attestation verify .\SysManager-v1.136.169.exe --repo laurentiu021/SystemManager
That proves which commit and workflow produced this exact binary, something the
SHA256 file cannot show, since it is published alongside the exe it describes.
Each release also ships SysManager-v1.136.169.sbom.json, a CycloneDX inventory of
every dependency resolved for this build, and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt, the
licenses and notices of the open-source components the exe carries, which About
also opens from the exe itself.
